title: ‘Bel-Air’ Spinoff ‘Hilary’ Starring Coco Jones in Development at Peacock
description:
A “Bel-Air” spinoff is in the works at Peacock.

	“Hilary,” an offshoot of the Will Smith-inspired drama series starring Coco Jones, is in developme
body:
A “Bel-Air” spinoff is in the works at Peacock.

	“Hilary,” an offshoot of the Will Smith-inspired drama series starring Coco Jones, is in development at the streamer. The project hails from writer-producer Tracy Oliver, co-writer of “Girls Trip” and “Little.”

	If the series moves forward, “Bel-Air” will become Peacock’s first scripted original series to get a spinoff.


	Jones played Will Smith’s (Jabari Banks) cousin Hilary Banks across all four seasons of “Bel-Air,” a dramatic reimagining of “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” that became a breakout hit for Peacock. The show followed Will Smith’s journey from the streets of West Philadelphia to the luxurious gated mansions of Bel-Air. (We all know the song…)
	

	The logline of “Hilary” reads, “After accepting an unexpected job offer from celebrity chef Yvonne Durand, Hilary Banks impulsively moves to New York determined to prove herself beyond her Bel-Air connections — only to find that success, friendship and love in the city come with a cost she never anticipated.”

	Jones and Oliver executive produce “Hilary” alongside Will Smith, Terence Carter, David Boorstein and Miguel Melendez of Westbrook Studios; Benny Medina, Andy Borowitz, Susan Borowitz, Morgan Cooper, the Jeff Pollack trust and the Quincy Jones estate.

	Deadline broke the news.

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Disney’s villains are getting some new bling just in time for spooky season.

	Disney and Pandora are expanding their long-running jewelry collaboration with a new collection inspired by three of the studio’s most recognizable villains: Scar from “The Lion King,” Lucifer from “Cinderella” and Lotso from Pixar’s “Toy Story 3.” The new charms arrive on Pandora’s website Thursday, Aug. 27, ahead of Halloween.



						
			
	

	
					

	The standout is Lotso, whose famously strawberry-scented exterior has been translated into Pandora’s first-ever scented charm. The piece recreates the deceptively cuddly “Toy Story 3” antagonist with his signature strawberry aroma, adding a sensory twist to the jeweler’s character-driven lineup.


	Scar, meanwhile, appears with the sweeping mane and imperious expression familiar from Disney’s 1994 animated classic, while Lucifer — Lady Tremaine’s scheming feline sidekick in “Cinderella” — gets a similarly mischievous character treatment.

	The trio joins an already extensive Disney x Pandora collection, which currently includes everything from princesses and “Lilo & Stitch” characters to existing Disney Villains pieces inspired by Maleficent and the Evil Queen. Pandora has also been steadily building out its Halloween assortment, with glow-in-the-dark ghosts and pumpkins alongside seasonal Disney releases.

	The wider assortment includes Jack Skellington, Sally and Zero from Tim Burton’s “The Nightmare Before Christmas,” as well as a pumpkin-costumed Stitch charm. Pandora’s current Disney Halloween lineup includes the new Sally charm, Jack Skellington and Zero pieces and a Stitch Halloween Pumpkin charm.


	The Scar, Lucifer and Lotso charms will be available beginning Aug. 27 at Pandora’s online store.

title: Veteran Hollywood Publicist Leonard Morpurgo Dies at 93
description: Leonard Morpurgo, the London-born international film publicist and communications executive who had senior posts at companies including Rogers & Cow
body:
Leonard Morpurgo, the London-born international film publicist and communications executive who had senior posts at companies including Rogers & Cowan, Universal Studios, Columbia Pictures, CBS Theatrical Films and Lorimar Pictures, died of cancer on Aug. 12. He was 93. 

	Morpurgo’s career spanned over 50 years. He worked at newspapers before becoming a publicist. A gentlemanly figure who was a fixture at film festivals and markets worldwide, he was fluent in multiple languages and specialized in sharing his global perspective while representing independent and major-studio film and television productions. His experiences and observations from the international film world formed the basis of his 2009 memoir “Of Kings and Queens and Movie Stars,” a collection of stories recalling encounters with figures in the entertainment industry including Cary Grant, Steve McQueen and Omar Sharif.
	

	“He was in one desert for the filming of ‘Lawrence of Arabia’ and another for ‘Dune,’” said his son, Thierry Morpurgo in a statement. “That was the kind of life he led — always close to the world of movies, wherever the work took him.”


	Morpurgo was a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and frequently participated on the Academy’s International Feature Film Committee. He also was a member of the British Academy of Film and Television Arts Los Angeles.

	In 2022, Morpurgo was nominated for the International Cinematographers Guild’s Les Mason Award for Achievement in Publicity, recognizing his longstanding contributions to the profession.
	

	“Leonard brought uncommon experience, intelligence, and perspective to every campaign and every conversation,” said longtime collaborator and president of Weissman/Markovitz Communications Rick Markovitz. “He was a skilled raconteur, and I will miss his passion for storytelling and hearing about the old days of Hollywood.”

	Morpurgo’s vast experience and enduring presence made him well-known as an international film publicity professional. 

	“Leonard was a sweet, kind and generous soul — and my second boss after I moved to Los Angeles nearly five decades ago,” said publicity executive Pamela Godwin-Austin. “He shared his knowledge generously and was a great mentor. He knew how to temper the pressures of the job with humor. I am grateful he showed me the way.”

	Along with his contributions to the film industry, Morpurgo was an accomplished needlepoint artist. In his final months, he took pleasure in seeing his work exhibited in a virtual-reality art gallery.

	Morpurgo is survived by his wife Elena-Beth Kaye, his twin sons Benjamin and Thierry, and his grandchildren, Violet, Oona and Lucien.

title: Shonda Rhimes Renews Netflix Overall Deal for Another Five Years
description: Shonda Rhimes is staying put at Netflix, with the superproducer and her Shondaland production banner renewing their overall deal with the streamer f
body:
Shonda Rhimes is staying put at Netflix, with the superproducer and her Shondaland production banner renewing their overall deal with the streamer for a further five years. 

	Rhimes and her producing partner, Betsy Beers, has been based at Netflix since 2017. 

	Bela Bajaria, Netflix’s chief content officer, said of the renewal, “I am thrilled to extend our partnership with the incomparable Shonda Rhimes. Few creative partnerships have shown what’s possible when a singular vision meets a global stage: stories that become genuine phenomena, shaping fashion, music and culture far beyond the screen. Nearly a decade in, this partnership keeps proving that Shonda’s instincts aren’t just brilliant storytelling — they’re a blueprint for what a hit can become. We couldn’t be prouder to remain the home where Shondaland continues to surprise and entertain audiences around the world.” 
	

	Shondaland’s biggest show to date on Netflix is “Bridgerton,” which recently aired its fourth season and has already been renewed for a fifth. It is one of the most popular show’s in Netflix history, with Seasons 1 and 3 ranking in the Top 10 Netflix shows of all time with 113.3 million views and 106 million views respectively. Per Netflix, Season 4 pulled in over 100 million views, while the streamer also previously aired the popular prequel series “Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story.” 


	“I am excited to extend our relationship with Netflix. For almost a decade, Netflix has provided Shondaland with the autonomy and support to tell our kind of stories—stories that both entertain and reflect diversity and humanity in a way that resonates with audiences around the world,” Rhimes said. “I am so thankful to Ted, Bela and the entire Netflix team for their continued partnership, trust and enthusiasm. Let’s GO!”
	

	In addition to serving as the exclusive home to Shondaland film and TV projects, the overall deal also covers gaming, merchandise, and live events connected to the IP. Netflix will also continue to support Shondaland’s inclusion initiatives like Ladder Program, to help train underrepresented below the line creatives.

	In addition to “Bridgerton,” Shondaland’s other projects with Netflix include the hit limited series “Inventing Anna” starring Julia Garner as Anna Delvey, the murder mystery “The Residence” starring Uzo Aduba, the Emmy-winning documentary “Black Barbie,” and “Dance Dreams: Hot Chocolate Nutcracker,” Shondaland’s documentary chronicling legendary choreographer and director Debbie Allen.

title: Shannon Wallace, Curtiss Cook, Lauren E. Banks, Liv Symone, Jason Dirden Join Starz Black Rodeo Drama
description: Shannon Wallace, Curtiss Cook, Lauren E. Banks, Liv Symone and Jason Dirden are set to join the cast of a Starz drama series within the world of Bla
body:
Shannon Wallace, Curtiss Cook, Lauren E. Banks, Liv Symone and Jason Dirden are set to join the cast of a Starz drama series within the world of Black rodeo in Southeast Texas.

	The untitled, one-hour series received an eight episode order in April. The drama is Starz’s second self-owned series following its 2025 spin off from Lionsgate. The other is British boxing drama “Fightland,” which premiered July 31 from executive producer Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson.
	

	The newly announced cast members join DeWanda Wise (“Three Women,” “Killing Faith”) as Anaya Clarke-Reagan, Tian Richards (“Tom Swift,” “Ballard”) as Rodney Clarke and Marcus Emanuel Mitchell (“Doctor Odyssey,” “Chicago Fire”) as Julius Calhoun.


	Wallace (“Diarra From Detroit,” “Beauty in Black”) plays Sebastian Clarke, described as “a former bull-riding champion whose career ended after a near-fatal arena accident.” Wallace is represented by Kimberly Hines, Matias Branger and Max Burbey at Luminary Partners and Cierra Carter at LaPolt Law.

	Cook (“The Chi,” “House of Cards”) plays Elias Clarke, said to be “the Clarke siblings’ estranged father and co-founder of the family rodeo who returns from prison to earn back his children’s trust.” Cook is represented by Harden Curtis Kirsten Riley Agency, Jordan Lee Talent and TCA MGMT.

	Banks (“Lawmen: Bass Reeves,” “City on a Hill”) stars as Wynter, “Sebastian’s ex-wife who is ready to finally do things for herself.” Banks is represented by CAA, Viewpoint and Del Shaw Moonves Tanaka Finkelstein Lezcano Bobb & Dang.
	

	Symone (“Power Book III: Raising Kanan,” “Michael”) is Jojo Calhoun, “the younger sister to local bull riding star Julius and a talented rapper.” Symone is represented by Stewart Talent and Brave Artists Management.

	Dirden (“Bosch: Legacy,” “Power Book III: Raising Kanan”) plays Greg Reagan, “a respected District Court judge and husband to Anaya who has a carefully hidden past.” Dirden is represented by Adam Lazarus Artists & Representatives and Amanda Hendon Entertainment 3:33.

	Kirk A. Moore is showrunner and executive producer. Mark Johnson and Myki Bajaj of Gran Via Productions and Tony Hernandez, Elise Henderson and Lilly Burns of Counterpart Studios also serve as executive producers. Giovanna Desselle, vice president of original programming, and Christina Jokanovich, senior vice president of original programming, are the executives overseeing the series for Starz.

title: Meghan Markle’s ‘The Gentlemen’ Rumors May Have Overshadowed Season 2 Launch — but Her Role Isn’t Off the Table
description: Plans for the phased rollout of “The Gentlemen” Season 2 had been in the works for months. Netflix‘s Sept. 3 launch date was set with all the usual
body:
Plans for the phased rollout of “The Gentlemen” Season 2 had been in the works for months. Netflix‘s Sept. 3 launch date was set with all the usual components in place for one of the streamer’s starry dramas: a trailer, a Season 3 renewal announcement, a junket, a press conference and a red-carpet premiere at a historic London venue followed by a glamorous afterparty — the perfect place to celebrate the latest installment of Guy Ritchie’s high-octane series about dukes and drug dealers.
	

	But in a case of life imitating art, the show’s entire publicity strategy was inadvertently wrecked by a real-life aristocrat, after reports leaked that Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, was being eyed for a role in the series. Just days ahead of Netflix’s long-planned release of a full-length trailer for the new season, in tandem with an announcement the show had been renewed, the leak dominated the news cycle for 24 hours. Then came a new report claiming her role had been canned due to the “backlash.”


	So what on Earth happened? And, more importantly, what’s actually true?

	Early Friday morning, a little-known Australian royal reporter called Bronte Coy claimed during a segment on Sky News Australia that Meghan, Duchess of Sussex was planning to “return to acting” and it was partly for this reason she and husband Prince Harry were relocating to the U.K. While Coy was, well, coy on details about the supposed project — whether it was a film or a TV show, a cameo role or series regular — she was adamant “there is a role in the works,” and that Meghan was about to sign on.
	

	As with anything related to Meghan and Harry, even the most gossamer threads of gossip quickly ignited, and news of Meghan’s mysterious new role spread across multiple continents. A few hours later, The Hollywood Reporter revealed the unnamed mystery project was at Netflix — despite Meghan and Harry’s rocky relationship with the streamer after the collapse of their reported $60 million deal — and was already in production in the U.K.

	That story set off a new round of frantic guesswork, and the streamer’s staff — both past and present — were inundated with queries from journalists trying to get a steer on which project. Was Meghan, who has publicly shared her dislike of the nude pantyhose favored by British royals, willing to don a corset for “Bridgerton”? Or would she dust off one of her suits from “Suits” for a knowing cameo on “The Diplomat,” an entire series about the fraught relations between the U.S. and the U.K.? Or had Charlie Brooker lined up some canny stunt casting with a “Black Mirror” episode about a duchess in dystopia?

	Forty minutes later, Deadline claimed to have the answer: Guy Ritchie’s “The Gentlemen,” an edgy series about aristocrats and criminals running a cannabis empire together, in which Theo James plays a duke opposite Kaya Scodelario’s underworld heiress. Curiously, that story, published on Friday, claimed the show hadn’t yet been renewed for a third season. In fact, although news of the Season 3 renewal was only officially announced two days later, everyone working on the series knew it was well into pre-production with cameras set to roll imminently.

	The real story behind Meghan’s potential appearance on the show, Variety has learned from a well-placed source with knowledge of the situation, is that it was an “incredibly nascent concept” — so nascent, it was hardly considered “real on any level.” Effectively, Ritchie threw out the duchess’ name while brainstorming ideas, well before the royal couple announced they were relocating back to the U.K. Meghan’s was just one of “a smorgasbord of names” Ritchie mentioned, says the source: there was certainly no suggestion of contracts about to be signed. The source was puzzled as to how Meghan had even heard about Ritchie’s suggestion unless she’d had direct conversations with him (if she did, the source wasn’t aware of them). The idea may also have been shared via their agents, since they’re both repped by WME.
	

	Ritchie has often gone for unusual casting choices, giving former soccer player Vinnie Jones his first ever acting role in 1998’s “Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels” at a time when it was much harder for non-actors to cross over into film. Jones also stars in “The Gentlemen” as the Halstead groundskeeper. 

	This season, Ritchie has also cast “Love Island” U.K. host Maya Jama in her first ever dramatic role, playing a fixer for a Middle Eastern tycoon. (“He would be like, ‘Yeah, you’re doing well’ and reassure me, which was really nice,” Jama told Variety of working with the director earlier this year). And while there aren’t many Americans in “The Gentlemen,” Giancarlo Esposito returns in Season 2 as mysterious U.S. billionaire Stanley Johnston, who could well have a daughter around Meghan’s playable age.

	Either way, no one in Meghan’s camp went out of their way to deny each report as it broke throughout Friday. Variety’s source suspects the story might even have been seeded by her reps — or further inflamed — given it helps acclimatize audiences to the idea of Meghan’s return to acting, not to mention signaling to producers she’s available. (On Sunday, The Times of London ran a story suggesting the “Gentlemen” story was “leaked to bolster her acting credentials.”) “I’m stunned if this isn’t coming from her [camp],” says Variety’s source. 

	So what to make of the subsequent claim on Saturday, published by former Vanity Fair editor and royals expert Tina Brown in her Substack newsletter, that the role had actually been offered and then withdrawn due to “backlash”? Well, Variety hears that’s not quite right either. If there is an offer, it’s not entirely dead. Scripts are still in the process of being written, so there could potentially be a role if Ritchie and co-writer Matthew Read want to make one work.

	Variety’s source wasn’t aware of a “backlash” per se, although acknowledged that Megan is polarizing, particularly to British audiences. But that’s not necessarily a career-killer in Ritchie’s eyes. “I wouldn’t rule out it happening,” the source says of where things currently stand.

	With Season 3 not likely to hit screens until 2028, Netflix is currently focused on getting through the launch of Season 2, which has now been somewhat overshadowed by all the rumors. “People are bummed,” the source acknowledges of the spotlight that’s shifted away from the show’s deserving cast and crew. Netflix publicists are preparing themselves for the fact that the upcoming junket, press conference and media line, all scheduled for next week, will probably be dominated by the duchess. On the bright side, it’s all publicity for the show.
	

	As for Ritchie, “I’m sure he loves this on some level,” says the source wryly. “He loves mayhem.”

title: ‘Warlock’ Stars Tricia Helfer, Maggie Robertson Break Down New ‘D&D’ Video Game Characters as First Gameplay Footage Is Revealed
description: The first gameplay footage from upcoming “Dungeons & Dragons” action-adventure game “Warlock” was revealed during Gamescom‘s Opening Night Live pres
body:
The first gameplay footage from upcoming “Dungeons & Dragons” action-adventure game “Warlock” was revealed during Gamescom‘s Opening Night Live presentation Tuesday.

	From “D & D” maker Wizards of the Coast and developer Invoke Studios, “Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons” is described as an original third person single-player action-adventure game that’s “set in a dark fantasy open world inspired by ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ where magic is a tool that players will use creatively across systemic combat and exploration.” 
	

	The “D&D” game, which is set to release in 2027, stars Tricia Helfer (“Battlestar Galactica,” “Lucifer”) as Kaatri, a veteran warrior who makes a pact to wield otherworldly magic against dark powers, and “Baldur’s Gate 3″ star Maggie Robertson as Kaatri’s patron, the witch queen Tasha, aka Iggwilv.


	“I think this game is different because we’re following one character’s story,” Robertson tells Variety. “With ‘Baldur’s Gate,’ you really got to choose your own adventure. You picked your party, and every playthrough could be completely different. Here we’re diving deeply into one character’s backstory, emotions, and motivations. That’s what makes it exciting — we’re focusing on the story and getting to know Kaatri. ‘Warlock’ takes us through the relationships of these specific characters, Tasha and Kaatri. Instead of being pulled in many different directions, we’re asking players to focus on one relationship with a lot of emotional depth.”

	Helfer adds: “But as Maggie mentioned, the game is very focused on Kaatri and her quest. Along the way, there’s also a wonderful team that joins her on the journey. We really get to understand her, know her motivations, and hopefully become captivated by the emotion driving her. And you’ll still have all the fun parts of D & D. You’ll still see iconic spells, characters, and locations from D & D. I think Warlock is trying to balance being a great experience that is both accessible to newcomers and longtime fans of D & D.”
	

	See below for Variety‘s full interview with “Warlock” stars Helfer and Robertson about their roles in the upcoming game, followed by the new gameplay footage trailer.
	
		How would you describe your characters?	

	Tricia Helfer: Well, Kaatri is a fighter and the warlock at the heart of this story. She gains her magic through a pact with Tasha, and her quest is very personal and urgent. There’s a timeline — she’s searching for someone, and it’s full of emotion. But she’s as I said, a warrior, and she’s a badass.

	Maggie Robertson: Tasha is awesome. And interesting. She’s one of the most iconic figures in D & D lore. She even has her own book, which is cool. She is this ancient and immensely powerful being. What’s fun about her is that she’s neither good nor evil. She straddles that line, so it’s fun to see where she chooses to fall at any given moment. You never know which version you’re going to get, and she always keeps you on your toes in that way. She’s warm and almost fairy godmother-like, but also dangerous. She has a real edge to her, and you definitely don’t want to get on her bad side. She’s helping Kaatri, but she also has her own agenda throughout the story. You’ll learn more about that as you go and see how they work together to achieve their own ends.
	
		Obviously, the big dynamic between a warlock and their patron is the pact they make. In creating these characters, how did you express that relationship through your performances and while working together on the game?	

	Helfer: As an actor, you often meet people just as you’re about to step onto set, and that’s what happened with us. But immediately I felt, “OK, this is somebody I can play with”. Maggie’s somebody I can play with, and I think we were very quickly on the same wavelength.

	Robertson: They threw us into the deep end with the scenes we had, too, because they were pages long — just talking, talking, talking.

	Helfer: Amazing what you had to pull off with all the spells and everything, but we got it all.It was also a great team to work with. Stefan, Catherine, and everybody doing the performance capture were fantastic.

	Robertson: It really helps when there’s a sense of collaboration, because everyone brings their own skills to the table. Collectively, we create something better than any one of us could have created alone. Getting to play together in the volume, having a creative team that encouraged discussion and experimentation, really helped us find the nuances in each scene. It would have been easy for every interaction to feel similar, so we had to ask ourselves, “What makes this scene different? What’s happening here that wasn’t happening in the previous one?” Even if some of the dialogue was similar, the emotional conversations were very different, and playing with those tonal shifts was a lot of fun.
	

	Helfer: Absolutely. And for me, the magic of filming was Kasper — the head writer.

	Robertson: Oh yeah.

	Helfer: Because he knows everything. When you’re filming, you’re not necessarily shooting in order, so sometimes you don’t know exactly where you are in the story. Unlike a traditional script that you’ve read from beginning to end, you’re thrown into scenes and thinking, “Where am I? What’s going on?” So I’d always look over to Kasper and ask, “What’s this? What’s happening here?”

	Robertson: Especially in D & D, where the lore is so massive. Having someone who could interpret all of that history — and explain what elements they were specifically pulling into this game — was incredibly helpful.
	
		You mentioned D & D lore. Obviously when people think about D & D, they think about parties, skill checks, rolling dice, and all those classic elements. How do you see Warlock being different from previous D & D adaptations like “Baldur’s Gate?”	

	Robertson: I think this game is different because we’re following one character’s story. With “Baldur’s Gate,” you really got to choose your own adventure. You picked your party, and every playthrough could be completely different. Here we’re diving deeply into one character’s backstory, emotions, and motivations. That’s what makes it exciting — we’re focusing on the story and getting to know Kaatri. “Warlock” takes us through the relationships of these specific characters, Tasha and Kaatri. Instead of being pulled in many different directions, we’re asking players to focus on one relationship with a lot of emotional depth.

	Helfer: But as Maggie mentioned, the game is very focused on Kaatri and her quest. Along the way, there’s also a wonderful team that joins her on the journey. We really get to understand her, know her motivations, and hopefully become captivated by the emotion driving her.

	And you’ll still have all the fun parts of D & D. You’ll still see iconic spells, characters, and locations from D & D. I think Warlock is trying to balance being a great experience that is both accessible to newcomers and longtime fans of D & D.
	
		How did you get involved with the project? Were you approached, or did you audition?	

	Helfer: Through the audition process!
	

	Robertson: I love this question because people always assume we have more power than we actually do. We audition, baby.

	Helfer: Yeah. When it’s a straight offer, you’re like, “Yes!” Those are rare. And honestly, even those can be stressful because you get to set thinking, “Nobody actually saw my interpretation beforehand.” For me, the audition process was pretty extensive. There were only two sessions, but the first was a Zoom audition that lasted about an hour. At the time, I was dating a fighter pilot who actually built me a belt so I could draw a sword from a sheath. I was just wearing jeans and a tank top, but having the sword made me feel like a badass instead of just standing in a room.
	
		Once it seemed like you were getting close to booking it, how did you start feeling about the character and the world?	

	Helfer: I didn’t have a full script — just a couple of scenes. Even those audition scenes changed somewhat from what we ultimately filmed. But from what I saw, I became really excited to play Kaatri. I really wanted to put myself into her skin.

	Robertson: Very different experience. I was doing self-tapes. Initially I read for different characters, then they asked me to audition for Tasha. My callback came while I had COVID. I recorded it anyway.
	
		Any final thoughts before we wrap up?	

	Helfer: We’re just so excited to reveal more of “Warlock” at Gamescom on August 25. There’s a gameplay reveal coming, which is both exciting and nerve-wracking. This is just the beginning — there’s so much more to come. We hope you love these characters.

	Robertson: We love them, and we hope you will too. We’re excited to share this story with you.

schema.headline: ‘Warlock’ Stars Tricia Helfer, Maggie Robertson Break Down New ‘D&D’ Video Game Characters as First Gameplay Footage Is Revealed

title: Haim Saban, Teddy Schwarzman and Lawrence Bender Among Those Condemning ‘Antisemitic’ Tropes in Mark Ruffalo’s Paramount Discourse: It ‘Puts Our Community in Grave Danger’
description: Haim Saban, Teddy Schwarzman and Lawrence Bender are among a group of industry figures who have put their names to a statement condemning “antisemit
body:
Haim Saban, Teddy Schwarzman and Lawrence Bender are among a group of industry figures who have put their names to a statement condemning “antisemitic theories” in Mark Ruffalo’s Paramount discourse.

	“Singling out Jewish executives and describing them in terms lifted from centuries-old antisemitic conspiracy theories, while invoking Israel as the frame for that attack, is antisemitic,” they say.


	Others putting their name to the statement include Ram Bergman, Anthony Bregman, Lynn Harris, Matti Leshem, Jamie Patricoff, Craig Emanuel, Shep Rosenman and Micah Green. The group have publicly endorsed the letter on behalf of a group of over a thousand Jews and allies in the media, music and entertainment industries.
	

	“This is not commentary on a merger. It is not a criticism of a government. This is simple antisemitism, where Jewish executives are portrayed as a secretive and powerful wealth-hoarding elite delighting in mass death,” the statement continues. “This is the same rhetoric that Nazis, Soviets, and the Klan weaponized against Jews, and its consequences are not only historical: they show up today in attacks against Jews in our streets, our synagogues, and our schools.”

	“This is a callous continuation of the ongoing campaign by the same individuals and groups targeting Jewish people and the state of Israel, a pattern of antisemitism and misinformation that puts our community in grave danger.”

	The statement was made amid the ongoing war of words between the Marvel actor, who is currently starring in the $2 billion-grossing “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” and Paramount Skydance, which is in the process of acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery.
	

	Ruffalo has been one of the most outspoken critics of the deal, spearheading numerous open letters, op-eds and social media posts opposing the acquisition.

	On Friday, however, many felt his relentless criticism of Paramount, which is headed by David Ellison, had crossed over into overt antisemitism when the four-time Oscar nominee posted a video clip of a Jewish Paramount board member Safra Catz speaking on a panel last year and urged his 21 million Instagram followers to “look how she revels in… genocide.” (Catz is former CEO of Larry Ellison’s tech company Oracle). In his commentary Ruffalo also said the Ellisons are “crushing workers and consolidating the wealth of the world for their own power.”

	Paramount responded robustly to his claims, saying it was “troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute.” Ruffalo fired back on X, calling the accusation “appalling and fundamentally dishonest.”

	Paramount’s statement was supported by the Simon Wiesenthal Center and Creative Communities for Peace. Hannah Einbeinder, Emmy-winning star of comedy “Hacks,” was among those who posted their support of Ruffalo.

	Read the full letter below:

	“We are writing on behalf of a group of nearly 1000 members, friends, and allies of the Jewish community who are proud to be working in film, television, music, Broadway, social and digital, and other platforms in and around the entertainment industry. It is unfortunate that we are yet again forced to state our unequivocal condemnation of the use of antisemitic tropes and narratives by those who use their platform for targeted hate speech toward Jews.

	Singling out Jewish executives and describing them in terms lifted from centuries-old antisemitic conspiracy theories, while invoking Israel as the frame for that attack, is antisemitic. It is unacceptable to introduce Jews, antizionism, or antisemitism into conversations about business transactions, simply because those involved are Jewish. There is nothing “strange” about a Jewish executive discussing substantive issues about tech.

	This is not commentary on a merger. It is not a criticism of a government. It is simple antisemitism, where Jewish executives are portrayed as a secretive and powerful wealth-hoarding elite delighting in mass death. This is the same rhetoric that Nazis, Soviets, and the Klan weaponized against Jews, and its consequences are not only historical: they show up today in attacks against Jews in our streets, our synagogues, and our schools.
	

	This is a callous continuation of the ongoing campaign by the same individuals and groups targeting Jewish people and the state of Israel, a pattern of antisemitism and misinformation that puts our community in grave danger.

	There is no excuse and no defense for this rhetoric, including the “I have Jewish friends” rationale, and there are many questions that demand an answer — including, is there someone behind the funding of this campaign that is continuously perpetrated by the same individuals?

	We will keep standing up against this hatred. Because when we say, NEVER AGAIN, we mean it.”

title: Dolly Parton’s Dollywood Will Be Open Wednesday After Singer’s Death: ‘The Show Must Go On’
description: Dollywood, the Tennessee theme park and resort owned by legendary country singer Dolly Parton, was closed Tuesday as previously scheduled. The compa
body:
Dollywood, the Tennessee theme park and resort owned by legendary country singer Dolly Parton, was closed Tuesday as previously scheduled. The company, in a statement after news of Parton’s death broke, said the park will be open Wednesday.

	“In her spirit, Dollywood will be open Wednesday as Dolly wanted, always reminding everyone with her signature sparkle — ‘the show must go on,'” the company said in a statement. “Together, we honor her by carrying forward her message of love, perseverance and hope.”
	

	But those trying to buy tickets online to get into the park were out of luck: The Dollywood website became overloaded Tuesday after word spread of her death and was inaccessible for more than two hours. “We are currently experiencing abnormally high volume,” a message on dollywood.com said. “We appreciate your patience and hope to be back online shortly.” Dollywood subsequently posted its statement on the site.


	In its statement, the company said, “With heavy hearts, the Dollywood family mourns the passing of our beloved Dreamer-in-Chief, Dolly Parton. Everyone at Dollywood shares the sorrow of countless people around the world touched by Dolly’s warmth, wisdom and generous spirit. Dolly’s heartfelt wish was that Dollywood always remain a place of joy, hope and togetherness — a space where families and friends could honor her memory, not with silence, but with laughter, music and shared dreams.”

	Parton was unable to attend the Aug. 14 opening of Dollywood’s brand-new NightFlight Expedition roller coaster due to ongoing “health issues.” The company has invested $50 million in NightFlight, its most expensive attraction to date. In a social-media post earlier Tuesday, Dollywood said the ride would be closed through Sunday, Aug. 30, because “the manufacturer has asked for additional time to adjust the timing of the ride’s turntable to ensure a quality experience for this unique part of the attraction.”
	

	Parton bought an interest in the Silver Dollar City Tennessee theme park in 1986, after which it was renamed Dollywood. The Dollywood Company operates the theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, which anchors the 150-acre destination, along with a dinner theater, Dolly Parton’s Stampede, Dollywood’s Splash Country waterpark and the Dream More Resort and Spa. Located in the Knoxville metropolitan area, it is now the biggest ticketed tourist attraction in Tennessee.

	“The greatest privilege of my life has been helping Dolly bring her dreams to life at Dollywood,” Eugene Naughton, president of Dollywood Parks & Resorts, said in a statement. “Dolly’s heart was as vast as the mountains she cherished, and her compassion knew no bounds. She inspired generations to dream boldly and love deeply. While we grieve her loss, we are honored and committed to carry her light forward. Her legacy will continue to shine in every melody sung, every smile shared and every dream kindled within these gates.”

	The Dollywood Company said fans who wish to give in honor of Parton may consider making a gift to the organization “she was so deeply passionate about,” Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library, which is dedicated to giving out free books to kids.

                                                                      |

                                  August 25, 2026
                                12:46 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Dolly Parton's loved ones are already making plans to honor the country music legend following her death ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Family sources tell TMZ ... a small ceremony is being planned in Nashville in the coming days. We're told the gathering is expected to be intimate, with Dolly's closest family and loved ones coming together to celebrate her remarkable life and legacy.
      
    
            Our sources say there are no solidified plans yet for a public funeral or celebration of life ... though it's still early.
      

            As we first reported, Dolly died Tuesday morning at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville after she was admitted to the hospital early Friday with kidney and autoimmune issues.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Dolly had been dealing with health complications in recent months, including immune system and digestive issues, kidney stones, and medication-related problems. She also canceled appearances and postponed her Las Vegas residency while focusing on her health.
      
    
            The singer, songwriter, actress, and philanthropist leaves behind an incredible career spanning more than six decades ... including timeless hits like "Jolene," "9 to 5" and "I Will Always Love You."
      
    
            Dolly's impact reached far beyond music, of course ... from Dollywood to her Imagination Library, which has provided millions of books to children around the world.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            She was married to Carl Dean for 58 years before his death in March 2025.
